title: Sorry, Marcos can’t keep his ‘very, very important guest’ waiting
summary: During the ASEAN-US Special Summit, Trump thanks Marcos for the warm welcome and praises his family’s genes. Outside of meeting venues and in parts of the country, crowds protest the US leader’s…

blocks.text: ASEAN CHAIR. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. speaks at an ASEAN-US Special Summit Dinner, at the Solaire hotel in Paranaque, Metro Manila, Philippines, November 17, 2026.
/Carlos Barria/REUTERS

During the ASEAN-US Special Summit, Trump thanks Marcos for the warm welcome and praises his family’s genes. Outside of meeting venues and in parts of the country, crowds protest the US leader’s arrival citing his policies and Pax Silica.

After closing the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit and Related Summits, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. still had a scheduled press conference as 2026 ASEAN chair on Tuesday, November 17.
Marcos presented the summit’s outcomes for over 20 minutes. Only one question was entertained.

The Philippine leader was about to consider taking one more, but he stopped himself. Apparently, at the back of his mind was US President Donald Trump, who just arrived in Manila while the ASEAN Summit came to a close. The official schedule was also running a bit late.
Marcos said that Trump was already “waiting for us to go to him” for the “very informal” ASEAN-US Special Summit.

“We asked the leaders to stay for a little longer so that we could have this ASEAN-US Summit, because the President of the United States was coming to the Philippines anyway for a [state] visit. And so we thought it would be a good idea that we stayed maybe another few hours longer so we could have the ASEAN-US Summit,” he told reporters.
“I can’t keep the President of the United States waiting, so I have to go. I’m sorry,” he told journalists before leaving the media center.
The grand planeside welcome ceremony for Trump that day befitted his status as the leader of the Philippines’ oldest and only treaty ally.

Dozens of dancers performed while students waved Philippine flags to greet him as a band played Trump’s signature song, the Village People’s “YMCA.” One observer said the scene was reminiscent of a field demonstration. The atmosphere and reception was the exact opposite of the mood back home after the Republican Party’s overwhelming defeat in the midterm elections — a scathing rebuke for Trump who is now considered a lame-duck president.
At the ASEAN-US Special Summit, held after the Trump’s first-ever meeting with Quadrilateral Security Dialogue or Quad leaders, Marcos described Trump as their “very, very important guest.”

In return, Trump thanked Marcos for the warm welcome and congratulated him on his ASEAN chairmanship. The US leader also reiterated his close ties with the President’s parents, the late dictator Ferdinand E. Marcos Sr. and Imelda Marcos, and even complimented Marcos on his good genes.

“I knew your parents very well, and they were great. I believe in genetics, and they did a good job. You have very good genetics. I can tell you that,” Trump said. The Marcos family fled to the US for exile after the ouster of the late dictator Ferdinand E. Marcos Sr.
Trump also complimented the President’s son, House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos, who was also present at the dinner. The two met earlier at the airport reception for Trump.

“I just met your son. He’s a beautiful young man. He’s got a great future. And it’s an honor to meet you, especially to meet you. Okay, you’ve done a good job. Your parents have done a very good job,” Trump said.
Outside summit venues and beyond Metro Manila, crowds have gathered for days. Not in awe of Trump but outrage over his policies and the US-led Pax Silica initiative.

Advocates reject the Pax Silica project, which seeks to secure supply chains for critical minerals and semiconductors through partnerships with other countries, because of its potential environmental impact and displacement of indigenous communities.
Protests are determined to get closer to Malacañang Palace on Wednesday, November 18, when Trump holds a bilateral meeting with Marcos.
Will Trump get to at least see — from the air, as he would be ferried to and from Malacañang by helicopter — the mass protests from below? – Rappler.com
